outline.description: This chapter sets the stage for understanding why accelerating attention is critical for modern AI and introduces the evolution from FlashAttention-2 to FlashAttention-3. It outlines the key hardware limitations of previous generations and defines the problem that this research solves.
subtopics: The role of attention in Transformer architectures and its scaling challenges with long-context data.
Evolution of FlashAttention: From FP16 optimization in FlashAttention-1 to parallelization in FlashAttention-2.
Hardware Landscape: Limitations of current GPUs (Ampere) compared to new architectures (Hopper), specifically focusing on Tensor Cores and Memory Accelerators.
The Core Bottleneck: Why 35% utilization is suboptimal and potential areas for improvement.
Objective of FlashAttention-3: Achieving 75%+ utilization via asynchrony, low-precision, and specialized hardware exploitation.
outline.chapter_title: Foundations: Hardware Architecture and Execution Models
outline.description: Students will explore the physical components that make FlashAttention-3 fast. This chapter details the specific capabilities of Hopper GPUs, explaining how different hardware subsystems interact to enable new software optimizations.
subtopics: Memory Hierarchy: Global Memory (HBM), L2 Cache, Shared Memory (SMEM), and Register Files.
Thread Hierarchy: Warps, Warpgroups, CTAs, and Shared Grid Partitioning.
Data Movement Accelerator: The Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) and its advantage over traditional CUDA copying.
Computational Core: Smarter Tensor Cores (WGMMA) and their asynchronous capability (decoupling from memory latency).
Low-Precision Formats: Understanding FP8 (e4m3/e5m2) constraints, throughput benefits, and layout assumptions.
Producer vs. Consumer Roles in Warp-Specialized Kernels.
outline.description: This chapter focuses on the first major technique introduced in the paper: separating data movement tasks from computation tasks. It explains how this separation eliminates stalling waits and improves pipeline throughput.
subtopics: The Problem with Synchronous Kernels: Explain how TMA latency previously caused-producer warps to wait for consumer warps to start treating or vice versa.
Warp Specialization Strategy: Redefining warpgroups as dedicated 'Producers' (doing TMA loads) or 'Consumers' (doing GEMMs).
The Circular Buffer Mechanism: Using shared memory buffers to link producer and consumer stages sequentially and continuously.
List-Based Parallelism vs. Data Locality: Managing concurrency when moving queries across multiple key-value blocks simultaneously.
Pingpong Scheduling Across Warp Groups: Overlapping data loads in one group while comput-ing in another.
